properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 4 at 2:39AM CDT until October 4 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out
20 NM...
Eastern Choctawhatchee Bay...
Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to
60 NM...
Western Choctawhatchee Bay...

* Until 400 AM CDT.

* At 238 AM CDT, strong thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from near Escambia
Bay Bridge to 8 nm southeast of Navarre Beach to 31 nm southeast of
Okaloosa Deep Water Reef, moving northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mary Esther, Fort Walton Beach, Highway 331 Bridge, Shalimar,
Destin, East Bay, Okaloosa Pier, Garcon Point Bridge, Navarre
Beach, and West Choctawhatchee Bay.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 3 at 8:35AM CDT until October 4 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by recent excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Along the West Fork Big Blue River in Southeastern York
County in east central Nebraska and Northwestern Fillmore County in
south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 824 AM CDT, the gauge along the West Fork Big Blue River north
of Grafton was at 12.7 feet, which was above minor flood stage of
11.0 feet. As a result, fairly widespread flooding of pastures
and fields immediately adjacent to the river continues, including
downstream through the McCool Junction area. Based on trends at
the Grafton gauge, water levels appear to have crested and have
started a very slow, gradual drop that should continue over the
next few days. However, it now appears that the river will likely
remain above flood stage until at least sometime on Sunday,
prompting this Warning to be extended out farther in time.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
